title: Somerset Council: Using Microsoft Copilot to improve productivity
summary: Somerset reports two to four hours saved weekly per Copilot user, with 75% reporting better focus and 53% finding work more enjoyable.
account: Somerset offered 300 Copilot licenses to staff and assessed their experiences after three months. Staff reportedly reduced meeting-minute work from 72 to 17 minutes and saved two to four hours weekly. Productivity and enjoyment results are self-reported. The stated 4–10x ROI is project-side valuation, not independently validated cash savings.
purpose: Explore whether Copilot improves staff productivity and work experience.

ratings.reason: Staff report less time spent on meeting notes and other tasks.
Staff report improved focus, productivity, and work experience. The duration of those improvements is unknown.

ai_role.statement: The source attributes transcription, note creation, and related task support to Copilot. Staff surveys, interviews, and usage data underpin reported time and work-experience improvements, without an independent causal evaluation.

evidence.citation: Council or project account published in the Local Government Association AI case-study bank. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Somerset Council: Using Microsoft Copilot to improve productivity

produced_by: The discovery pilot provided 300 licenses to staff volunteers and used regular review points.
Participants received peer support through a Teams community and regular contact sessions.
must_hold: The conditions needed to reproduce the benefit are unspecified.

headline: Somerset reports time savings and improved staff focus
claim_basis: Sources: the deployer's report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
